messages.author: cee4e2fe6ae473ca
messages.subject: user specified environmental rasters
parts:
Hi everybody,
I'm trying to load environmental layers in wallace to make an SDM for the european nightjar.
All rasters (.tif) got exactly the same extent (after clipping rasters in ArcGIS), cell size (0.00021...), "projection".
Three are integer rasters (DEM, landcover, terrain ruggedness index) the other layers are floating point (eastness, northness, slope, precipitation, temperature).
When I load the files range values for floating point layers is not recognised (returns ?)
The range value for integer rasters is misread (unbelievable numbers around 0).
Not surprisingly "maxnet" fails to produce models, see the output below:

*** Running ENMevaluate using maxnet v.0.1.2 ***
Doing user-defined evaluation groups...
There are 3 background records with NA for at least one predictor variable.
                  Removing these records from analysis, resulting in 9997 records...

 7173 grid cells found with at least one NA value: these cells were excluded from raster predictions.
Warning: Error in [: (subscript) indice logicol troppo lungo
  95: regfun
  94: maxnet::maxnet
  93: modelTune.maxnet
  92: tuning
  91: ENMeval::ENMevaluate
  90: <reactive> [modules/mod_c6_maxent.R#94]
  74: mod.maxent
  73: observeEventHandler [C:\Users\UX580GEBN070R\Documents\R\win-library\4.0\wallace\shiny/server.R#519]
   2: shiny::runApp
   1: run_wallace

I tried to use maxent.jar, instead, but rJava and Rtools are not currently supported in R 4.0. 

Just for comparison, when I try some bioclim environmental layers, clipped to Italy, all works well.

I'll appreciate if you could give me suggestions. Please (sorry for that) remember I'm not a very much skilled R user...

Thank you in advance!

mario

Sorry, I forgot to ask if wallace could handle categorical raster data and, if it could, how do I have to instruct the software to recognize categorical from numerical environmental data sets?
regards
mario

messages.subject: Re: user specified environmental rasters
parts:
Browsing similar problems and answers I'd like to add that:
a) I did a stack of environmental rasters and no problems were detected;
b) I resampled rasters from ca. 20 m pixels to ca. 100 m pixels, to eventually prevent memory issues
c) in ENMeval I read both original and resampled rasters and the rasters seem to have no problems, moreover raster values are correctly read now;
d) from Rstudio I ran ENMevaluate and it did work (with 100 m rasters, not with 20 due to memory issues)
e) tried once again in wallace with 100 rasters, which are misread and step 6, model, freeze.

That's all at the moment!

regards

mario

messages.author: d73691b565754184
messages.subject: Re: user specified environmental rasters
parts:
Hi Mario,

Thanks for reporting this issue!

First, the current version of Wallace can not handle categorical variables, but this feature is included in the upcoming release of Wallace.

Second, my first thought after reading your first message is that something is wrong with your rasters because of the number of grid cells found with at least one NA value. After reading your last message, I'm not sure what is going on because you were able to run ENMevaluate without a problem. Maybe, this is an internal Wallace issue about using floating rasters, or it is a problem in handling NA default raster values (they are different between integer and floating) To figure out if this is happening, I have some questions for you:

1) After using the resampled 100 m rasters on Wallace (point e), were you getting the same error in the console?
2) Which parameters did you specify when you run ENMevaluate? Were the settings similar to the options that you are using on Wallace?
3) How did you know that rasters are misread on Wallace? I guess that it was after reading the raster in Step 3.
4) Were you getting misread values in the stack created on R?

I'm curious to figure out the issue and fixed if it is necessary.

Best,
Gonzalo
